title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
1 研究问题
当一个模型报告的估计定价误差更小时，究竟是什么变了？这一估计能否帮助使用者选择或改进收益预测？
定价误差（alpha）是股票预期收益中未被因子基准解释的部分（第 2.1 节，式 (1)）。实践中，预期收益和因子都需要估计，因此报告的 alpha 变小，可能是因子解释得更多，也可能是被解释的预期收益本身变了。本文先把这两种情况分开，再追问两个实际问题：alpha 的大小能否帮助选择预测？alpha 成分本身在预测中有没有用？

title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
2 为什么重要
“估计的 alpha 更小”常被用来论证新模型更好。如果差距主要来自拟合均值的变化，那么这一论证说的是信号，而不是因子。

经济含义。 alpha 总是相对于某个基准、信息集和期限而言。不固定被解释的信号就比较两个估计值，等于把两个不同的对象混在一起。
实务含义。 研究团队要在不同预测之间做选择，也要决定保留多少模型的 alpha 成分。这两者都是预测决策，都可以用之后的收益来检验。
统计含义。 估计的 alpha 带有估计噪声。全部保留可能增加误差，全部舍弃又可能丢掉信号。哪种效应占上风，只有在样本外做匹配比较才能回答。

title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
3 论证脉络


问题。 估计的 alpha 变小，是因子更好，还是拟合均值变了？→ 研究问题
动机。 模型比较、预测选择和 alpha 的使用，都取决于能否正确解读这个数字。→ 为什么重要
框架。 在相同股票、相同权重下，把每个拟合均值拆成载荷空间能生成的因子部分和特征截距部分。→ 理论框架
机制。 把两个拟合均值与两个载荷空间交叉组合：换空间，残差几乎不动；换均值，残差大幅变化。→ 一个简单例子；表 1
证据。 按残差大小选择预测帮助不大：按自身均值总是选 VW，按共同目标选择的平衡准确率低于 50%（第 5.1 节）。只保留截距部分的一个估计比例，在 24 个设定中有 20 个优于完整预测，但只有 8 个优于等权预测平均、6 个优于特征主成分校准（表 G.1）。→ 图 3
贡献。 用同一套匹配设计，把解释 alpha、用 alpha 做选择、在预测中使用 alpha 这三个问题分开。→ 与既有文献的比较
边界。 这是针对缩尾后次月收益的探索性证据，不是定价误差检验，也不是交易结果。→ 适用范围

title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
4 理论框架
先从经济对象出发。在时点 t，给定一组股票的预期超额收益 \mu_t、因子暴露 \beta_t 和风险价格 \lambda_t，定价误差为

\alpha_t = \mu_t - \beta_t \lambda_t .

它以月收益为单位（式 (1)），既不是已实现的噪声，也不等于错误定价的证据。
实证模型是工具化主成分分析（IPCA）式的基于特征的潜在因子模型 (Kelly 等 2019)：股票特征通过载荷矩阵 B 生成因子暴露，同时生成一个截距（式 (2)）。模型的拟合均值系数 \hat h 可以拆成因子部分 p 和特征截距部分 r：

\begin{aligned}
\hat h &= \underbrace{P_Q(B)\,\hat h}_{p:\ \text{因子部分}} + \underbrace{[I - P_Q(B)]\,\hat h}_{r:\ \text{特征截距部分}},\\
h(\eta) &= p + \eta\, r,\qquad \eta \in [0,1].
\end{aligned}

P_Q(B) 把系数投影到载荷空间上，即模型暴露所能生成的全部收益信号。Q 是特征格拉姆矩阵：两组系数差多少，就看它们对所研究股票的预测差多少，权重可以是等权（EW）或市值加权（VW）（第 2.2 节，式 (3) 至 (5)）。在给定的因子位置约定（即因子均值如何设定）下，r 恰好等于模型拟合出的特征 alpha（第 2.3 节，式 (6)）。如果用一个模型的空间去解释另一个模型的均值，剩下的是投影残差，而不是 alpha。
式子的后半部分对应预测使用决策：保留因子部分，只保留截距部分的一个比例 \eta（式 (14)）。\eta = 1 即完整预测，\eta = 0 则只剩因子部分。用过去的预测误差来确定 \eta，论文称之为“残差校准”；这里的“残差”指模型自身的截距部分 r，而不是跨模型的投影残差。本文属于特征几何这一研究脉络，另见《因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断》 (Liu 2026) 和《基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架》。

6 研究设计与主要结果
数据是与 Jensen 等 (2023) 特征库相对应的美国股票面板：153 个特征、749 个形成月（1963 年 7 月至 2025 年 11 月），预测对象是次月超额收益，并按每月第 1 和第 99 百分位做缩尾处理（第 3.1 节）。同一模型在相同股票上训练两次：一次等权（EW），一次按市值加权（VW）。在 2017 年 3 月至 2025 年 3 月的九个年度起点发布预测，目标月为 2017 年 4 月至 2025 年 12 月，共 105 个月；训练所用的收益始终早于被预测的收益（第 3.2 节）。预测精度用相对于零预测的预测 R^2 衡量，与 Gu 等 (2020) 的做法一致（式 (11)）。

这说明什么。 在等权度量下，两个模型各自的 alpha 分别为 117.37 和 77.27 bp。固定 EW 均值、只换空间，残差仅下降 0.70 bp；固定 EW 空间、换成 VW 均值，残差降至 75.02 bp（第 4 节；表 1）。对称分解把平方差距的约 101% 归于均值、−1% 归于空间；在市值加权度量下分别为 98% 和 2%（第 4 节）。这些是平方差距的份额，并非因果效应；−1% 表示空间的变化略微抵消了均值的变化。在每个年度起点重复交叉组合，等权度量下均值的份额在 96.8% 至 100.9% 之间（第 4.1 节；表 E.4）。VW 训练更看重大盘股的拟合，两种训练得到的均值估计差别很大；而两个空间对同一信号的表示能力相近。这一结果说明差距从何而来，但不说明哪个均值更接近真实值。

2. 差距能否帮助选择预测？ 在每个起点，发布历史残差更小的那个模型的预测。若用各模型自己的均值，这一规则在全部九个起点都选 VW 训练的模型，除了“永远选 VW”之外没有提供任何信息（第 5.1 节）。更公平的做法是用同一个目标来评判两个空间：在同一段历史上拟合的岭回归（即对特征做收缩回归来预测收益）。这样得到的选择会变化，图 2 检验的正是这些选择。


图 2：诊断优势与随后的预测差异。 九个年度起点，共同岭回归目标（图 2）。



读图说明。零点右侧表示诊断偏向 VW；零点上方表示 VW 随后预测得更好。位于右上或左下象限的圆点是判断正确，叉号是判断错误。来源：Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors，工作论文，2026 年 9 月，图 2；论文源文件中的 diagnostic_margins.pdf。

3. 这一成分在预测中是否有用？ 保留一个模型，只决定保留多少截距部分。比例 \eta 用此前十二个已完成的预测月估计，限制在 [0, 1] 内，再用于下一年：共八次决策、93 个目标月，2018 年 4 月至 2025 年 12 月（第 6.2 节）。

title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
7 与既有文献的比较
本文建立在基于特征的因子模型以及这一框架下关于定价误差的新近研究之上，评价标准则借鉴收益预测与预测组合两支文献。









既有研究
已有结论
本文的补充




Kelly 等 (2019)
用特征作为因子载荷的工具变量；截距刻画与特征相关、但并非来自因子暴露的收益。
沿用这一框架，追问拟合截距大小的变化究竟反映了什么。


Zhang (2024)
在潜在因子、以特征为协方差的设定下，设定并检验定价误差。
不提出新检验，而是对拟合对象及其预测用途做匹配比较。


Choi and Yuan (2025)
对“内部”和“外部”alpha 的估计与推断，含去偏处理。
回答不同的问题：报告的拟合 alpha 下降意味着什么。本文不对这些估计量作优劣比较。


Kim 等 (2021)
先把特征预测的收益归于因子载荷，再用与载荷正交的剩余部分构建套利组合。
从预测角度提出类似问题：发布的收益预测应保留多少特征截距成分，并与简单对照比较，不涉及组合收益。


Kozak 等 (2020)
对基于大量特征组合的随机贴现因子施加收缩先验，样本外表现良好；少数主成分比少数特征更能概括横截面。
把岭回归作为预测基准，并把部分保留 alpha 成分视为一个单独、可检验的收缩决策。


Pástor and Stambaugh (2000)
从投资后果的角度比较定价模型。
在共同任务上从预测决策的角度比较，不涉及投资组合结论。


Bates and Granger (1969)
在平方损失下，组合预测可以优于其中任一成分。
说明为什么等权平均是检验选择规则和校准规则的严格对照。




本文的切入点刻意收窄。使这些对象可以相互比较的恒等式，与作者的相关研究 (Liu 2026) 相同；本文的新增贡献是实证性的：在相同股票、相同日期和相同损失函数下，用一套设计把残差比较容易混淆的三个问题分开。估计的 alpha 的大小由什么决定？它能否帮助选择预测？这一成分在预测中是否有用？三个答案各不相同：主要是均值；帮助不大；有时有用。论文同时报告了不利的结果和窗口反转。

title: 如何解读估计的定价误差：来自基于特征的收益预测的证据
text:
8 适用范围

不是定价误差检验。 这些比较并不检验总体 alpha 是否为零（附录 I.2）。
不是交易结果。 预测对象是缩尾后的次月超额收益；预测 R^2 不是组合收益，也没有考虑交易成本和约束（附录 I.3）。
不是独立证据。 九次年度选择和 24 个相互重叠的设定只是敏感性汇总，既不是独立重复，也不是置信区间（第 3.4 节；附录 I.2）。
不涵盖所有 alpha。 研究对象是在给定约定下由特征生成的截距，而不是每只股票层面的全部定价误差。
探索性的历史证据。 样本期参与了研究设计的形成，原始收益数据版本也尚未完全核对一致（第 3.2 节；附录 I.3）。

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
1 研究问题
当公司特征彼此相关、尺度不一时，哪些特征组合构成因子模型中被定价的子空间，哪些只是冗余或残差？
如今，预期收益往往同时与几十个特征挂钩。主成分分析（PCA）、工具化主成分分析（IPCA）(Kelly 等 2019) 以及许多机器学习估计量，都以单位矩阵来度量特征空间中的长度与正交（论文第 1.1 节）。这一选择鲜少被明确交代。本文将其明确提出，并追问：若尺子取自数据，结论会有何不同？

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
2 为什么重要
尺子决定了什么算“不同”。在普通尺子下，两个载荷向量可以相互垂直，却挑中同一批股票。估计量于是可能把一个被定价的方向拆成两个因子，或让潜在因子复制模型中已有的可观测基准因子（论文第 1.1 节）。

经济含义。 哪些方向获得风险溢价、多少定价留给截距，都取决于用哪把尺子区分方向（论文第 1.1 节）。
实务含义。 若把潜在因子当作新的风险来源，使用者可能在不知不觉中把同一基准暴露持有两次。
统计含义。 样本内拟合揭示不了这个问题。在文中的模拟里，即便 IPCA 估出的潜在子空间离真值很远，其收益 R² 仍在 0.94 到 0.99 之间（论文第 7.3 节；表 9）。

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
3 论证脉络


问题。 当特征的相关性与尺度被认真对待时，哪些特征组合被定价？→ 研究问题
动机。 普通尺子会让同一个被定价方向被拆分、重复计入，或被截距吸收。→ 为什么重要
框架。 以长期特征度量衡量方向，并在该度量下写出归一化、模块间正交与无套利上界；由此得到的估计量称为无套利 IPCA（NA-IPCA）。→ 理论框架
机制。 普通尺子下相互垂直的方向，在特征尺子下可能彼此重叠；在这把尺子下划分模块，可以避免重复计算。→ 一个简单例子
证据。 美国股票的特征度量高度不均匀；在据此校准、且被定价方向与特征度量一致的模拟中，NA-IPCA 恢复了潜在子空间，不含截距模块的 IPCA 与 PCA 则没有。→ 研究设计与主要结果
贡献。 度量本身成为识别的明确对象；IPCA 是“尺子平坦、不设上界”的特例。→ 与既有文献的比较
边界。 证据限于特征几何与模拟；完整的资产定价应用留待配套研究。→ 适用范围

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
4 理论框架
设 Z_t 为第 t 月 N_t 只股票的 L 个特征。文中的尺子是长期特征度量（论文第 2 节）：

Q_Z = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{1}{N_t} Z_t^{\top} Z_t .

它是各月特征格拉姆矩阵的长期均值，刻画特征在股票之间如何共同变动。在这把尺子下，系数向量 a 的长度为 (a^{\top} Q_Z a)^{1/2}，大致衡量它所生成的暴露在股票之间差异有多大。若两个方向所生成的特征投资组合长期不共同变动，二者在该度量下即为正交（论文第 2 节）。
预期超额收益分为三个模块（论文第 2 节）：

\mathbb{E}_t\!\left[r_{t+1}\right] = Z_t\left(\Gamma_\beta f_t + \Gamma_\delta F^{\text{obs}}_t + \Gamma_\alpha\right).

\Gamma_\beta 是潜在因子 f_t 的载荷，\Gamma_\delta 是可观测因子（如可交易的基准因子）的载荷，\Gamma_\alpha 是由特征驱动的截距（论文表 1）。所有约束都在 Q_Z 下表述：潜在载荷在 Q_Z 下标准正交（\Gamma_\beta^{\top} Q_Z \Gamma_\beta = I）；可观测因子模块与截距模块都与潜在子空间正交；截距的大小 \Gamma_\alpha^{\top} Q_Z \Gamma_\alpha 不超过上界 \delta。\delta 越小，越接近严格无套利（论文第 2 节）。
估计量称为无套利 IPCA（NA-IPCA），即限制在该约束集上的加权最小二乘，其解由投影到约束集切空间上的加权最小二乘方程刻画（论文命题 3.1）。当尺子平坦且不设上界时，它退化为统计 IPCA（论文第 8 节）。文章还在所列条件下，为已识别的子空间推导了旋转不变的渐近推断（论文第 4 节）。

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
6 研究设计与主要结果
论文先在 Kelly 等 (2019) 的复制数据上估计 Q_Z：37 个经秩变换的特征（含常数项）、12,813 家公司、1964 年 7 月至 2014 年 5 月共 599 个月（论文第 6.1 节；表 2）。随后模拟 1,000 只股票、240 个月的面板，特征按该度量生成；设计中有三个位于 Q_Z 主导方向上的潜在因子，以及两个刻意设为弱因子的可观测因子（论文第 7.1 节；表 7）。模拟重复 300 次，比较 NA-IPCA、不含截距模块的 IPCA 与 PCA（论文脚注 11）。


图 2：特征尺子远非“正圆”。Q_Z 前 15 个主成分的方差占比。



读图说明。每根柱对应特征度量的一个主方向；若尺子是“正圆”，37 个方向各占约 3%。本页转载的论文原图保留英文坐标轴与标题。来源：SSRN 预印本，2026 年 3 月，图 2，第 33 页（转载自论文）。 论文原页



这说明什么。 第一主成分占特征离散度的 25%，前五个合计 62%；若尺子平坦，每个方向约占 3%（论文第 6.2 节；表 5）。特征值从 0.002 到 1.0，条件数为 502（论文表 2）。许多原始特征只是少数几种特质的不同版本：规模、价值、盈利、投资与动量各自形成紧密的簇（论文第 6.2 节）。从统计上看，普通尺子让近乎冗余的组合与真正区分公司的方向享有同等权重；论文把这几个离散度高的方向解读为最有能力承载风险补偿的方向（论文第 1.1 节）；但仅凭几何本身并不能说明哪些方向被定价。



图 3：当被定价方向与特征度量一致时，NA-IPCA 能恢复潜在子空间，IPCA 与 PCA 则不能。几何校准模拟中，估计的载荷子空间与真实子空间之间的距离。



读图说明。距离为 \lVert \sin\Theta \rVert_F，由估计子空间与真实子空间之间的夹角构成：完全恢复时为 0；估计子空间与真实子空间正交时取最大值，潜在因子模块（三个方向）为 \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73，可观测因子模块（两个方向）为 \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41（论文脚注 10）。数值越小越好。来源：SSRN 预印本，2026 年 3 月，图 4，第 39 页；表 8，第 38 页（转载自论文）。 论文原页



这说明什么。 就潜在子空间而言，NA-IPCA 的距离为 0.011，IPCA 为 0.73，PCA 为 0.99（论文表 8）。IPCA 还让潜在因子模块与可观测因子模块相互重叠：重叠度为 0.069，NA-IPCA 仅为 0.0005（论文表 8）。这正是简单例子中的重复计算，只不过发生在按美国数据校准的 37 个特征的模拟面板里。在可观测因子模块上排序反转：IPCA 的距离为 0.23，NA-IPCA 为 1.40，接近两个方向的最大值 1.41（论文表 8）。文章将此解读为 NA-IPCA 不为刻意设弱的可观测因子定价（论文第 7.2 节）。

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
7 与既有文献的比较
本文处在三支文献的交汇处：大面板因子模型、对因子施加经济约束的研究，以及随机贴现因子（SDF）的收缩与机器学习估计（论文第 1.2 节）。每一支都推进了因子模型可识别内容的边界。下表列出最接近的参照。









既有研究
已确立的结论
本文的推进




近似因子模型 (Bai and Ng 2002)
在弱相关条件下，确定大面板中公因子的个数
在因子个数给定之后，追问哪些方向构成被定价子空间，并用估计出的度量来衡量


IPCA (Kelly 等 2019)
以特征作为工具变量刻画时变 beta；同一框架已包含由特征驱动的截距与可观测因子，并检验二者是否为零
在 Q_Z 下写出归一化以及潜在因子模块、可观测因子模块与截距模块之间的分离，并为截距设上界；采用欧氏归一化、不设上界的 IPCA 是其特例


RP-PCA (Lettau and Pelger 2020)
在 PCA 中加入定价误差惩罚，使因子同时拟合平均收益
把定价约束放进可行集，借助度量与截距上界来实现


弱因子与伪因子 (Bryzgalova 2015)
与收益协方差很弱的因子可能呈现虚假的显著性，并挤出真实风险
把弱因子问题引入特征空间：论证普通尺子会让弱而冗余的方向吸收变动，并在模拟中设置弱可观测因子


近似无套利界 (Kozak 等 2018)
若不存在近似套利机会，SDF 可由少数几个高方差主成分很好地近似
在特征度量下，直接对截距模块施加类似的上界


收缩横截面 (Kozak 等 2020)
以先验收缩特征投资组合上的 SDF 系数，对低方差主成分收缩最强
不把特征度量用作惩罚项，而是用它定义模型的归一化与各模块之间的分离


波动率界 (Hansen and Jagannathan 1991)
资产价格约束了任何有效 SDF 的波动率
受其启发，在同一度量下对截距模块的定价含量施加二次上界




本文的切入点是尺子。许多既有研究是在几何已经固定的因子提取之上，再施加定价约束（论文第 1.2 节）。本文把特征度量变成一个明确的、需要估计的对象：在该度量下写出归一化、模块间正交与残差上界，并给出相应的估计量与推断。证据支持的是一个具体结论，而不是方法之间的总体排名：当特征分布不均、彼此相关时，尺子的选择会改变模型识别出的方向。后续论文《因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断》在度量需要估计的情形下，进一步发展了识别与推断部分。

title: 基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架
text:
8 适用范围

本文并未表明 NA-IPCA 能更好地预测收益或构建组合。其证据是特征空间的几何与校准模拟；完整的资产定价应用留待配套研究（论文第 8 节）。
模拟中，真实潜在载荷位于 Q_Z 的主导方向上（论文第 7.1 节）。结果说明的是普通尺子遇到这种几何时会出什么问题，而不是所有市场都具有这种几何。
模拟中的 IPCA 基准是不含截距模块的受限版本，而模拟收益中含有截距模块（论文第 7.1–7.2 节）。因此，这一比较并非单独检验尺子本身的作用。
Q_Z 是对单一样本（1964 至 2014 年）的估计描述；若特征分布发生变化，应重新估计（论文第 8 节）。
渐近结果依赖文中列明的正则性、识别与中心化条件（论文第 4 节）。本页不将其表述为一般性的渐近有效性（efficiency）结论，也不表述为 Le Cam 意义下的局部渐近正态性。
截距模块是模型中受约束的残差成分，并非实测的错误定价或 alpha。

title: 特征库与投资组合决策
text: 论文及网络附录（PDF，87 页，英文） · BibTeX

title: 特征库与投资组合决策
text:
1 研究问题
特征库在不增加信息的情况下发生变化时，经调参的投资规则是否仍会改变？这种改变能否进一步传导至持仓和净收益？
复制一列特征既不增加观测，也不改变可以构造出来的线性组合集合。但带正则的估计量按系数收取惩罚，复制之后，同一主题的暴露变得“更便宜”，即使重新选择惩罚参数也是如此（引言；第 I.B 节）。本文在四种经调参的组合方法中度量这一效应的大小，并将其从估计权重逐层追溯至经济主题、个股和扣除成本后的收益。

title: 特征库与投资组合决策
text:
2 为什么重要
管理人会例行更新特征库（引言）。常用的 Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen 特征库有 153 个特征、13 个主题（第 II.A 节），而各主题内部的重叠程度差别很大：质量主题有 17 列，其相关矩阵的参与秩却只有 3.47，大致相当于数据中独立方向的个数（并非独立信息来源的个数）；季节性主题有 12 列，参与秩为 11.78（论文第 III.A 节；表 II）。如果回测变好可能来自输入的“写法”而非输入的“内容”，那么评估特征库更新就需要另一种检验。

经济含义。 管理人看到组合更偏向价值主题，可能以为这是关于价值的新证据，其实其中一部分只是特征库的记账效应。
实务含义。 主题倾向的变化会转化为交易，而交易有成本。因此，即使毛收益几乎不变，表示方式的变化也可能改变净收益。
统计含义。 测试误差下降并不证明新输入带来了新信息。经调参的规则也可能仅仅因为惩罚变了而表现更好。

title: 特征库与投资组合决策
text:
3 论证脉络


问题。 不增加信息的特征库调整，会不会改变经调参的投资规则？→ 研究问题
动机。 特征库更新是日常工作，而通常用来评价它的回测无法区分新信息与重新赋权。→ 为什么重要
框架。 精确复制与主题缩放固定了数据和可达组合，因此任何反应都只能归于拟合程序本身。→ 理论框架
机制。 把一个主题复制若干份，相当于把它的有效岭惩罚除以份数，拟合随之偏向这个主题。→ 一个简单例子
证据。 主题再平衡使主题归因变动 0.20–0.27，个股目标持仓变动平均总敞口的 19%～28%（论文表 I）；净收益的变化取决于方法和成本；特征从 39 个实际扩到 153 个，对预测的影响小且不确定。→ 研究设计与主要结果
贡献。 一套实证诊断：把特征库更新沿主题归因、持仓和依赖成本的收益逐层追踪。→ 与既有文献的比较
边界。 这是诊断性研究：不主张可投资的业绩，也不给出最优特征库。→ 适用范围

title: 特征库与投资组合决策
text:
4 理论框架
研究设计固定投资方法、可投资股票和决策日期，只改变特征库（引言）。两种受控调整都不增加信息。选择性复制把某一主题的每一列变成共五份。主题再平衡（即按主题重新加权，并非调仓交易）按各主题的列数重新缩放各列，使列数多的主题不再比列数少的主题在惩罚下获得更大的活动空间。机制只需一行代数：若一个特征被替换为 m 个完全相同的列，其系数 \theta_j 之和为 b，那么在这一约束下，平方惩罚的最小值为

\min_{\sum_j \theta_j = b} \; \sum_{j=1}^{m} \theta_j^2 \;=\; \frac{b^2}{m}.

也就是说，对副本施加岭惩罚时，同样的暴露只收取原来 1/m 的“价格”（第 I.B 节，式 2）。对股票岭回归，存在一个精确对照：把副本的惩罚按比例调回（即“迁移”惩罚），原来的估计问题就完全恢复（第 I.B 节）。
所有估计都映射回原始的 153 个特征，并在同样的 13 个主题下计分（第 III.B 节）。一个主题的权重定义为它在拟合收益方差中的份额：

s_g = \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(u_g, u)}{\operatorname{Var}(u)},

其中 u_g 是主题 g 的收益，u 是总收益。各份额之和为一；当某主题起对冲作用时，份额可以为负（第 I.D 节，式 4）。归因变化取份额绝对变化之和的一半。文章把它与个股目标持仓的变化、扣除成本后收益的变化并列比较，因为三者衡量的是不同层面的后果。

收缩与正则化已是用大量特征构建组合的标准工具。最接近的研究是在给定特征库上比较方法；本文则固定每种方法，只改变特征库的写法。









既有研究
已有结论
本文的补充




Kozak 等 (2020)
对特征组合权重进行收缩，可得到样本外稳健的随机贴现因子。
说明同类惩罚会对特征库的表示方式作出反应，并把这种反应追踪到持仓。


Kelly 等 (2026)
UPSA 将多个岭回归组合加以集成，以优化样本外表现，并把权重归并到经济主题。
固定 UPSA 的公开代码、只改变其输入；再平衡使 UPSA 主题份额的变动距离达 0.274（论文表 I）。


Jensen 等 (2023)
构建了 153 个特征、13 个主题的特征库，多数因子可以复现。
以该特征库本身为研究对象：主题内部重叠不均，正是设置对照的动机。


Jensen 等 (2026)
组合应以扣除交易成本后的表现评价；考虑成本的学习方法能改进可实施前沿。
用固定且未作成本优化的配置规则和明确的成本账簿，说明特征库调整会传导到净收益；像该文那样考虑成本的优化器可能改变这一反应（第 IV.A 节）。


Choueifaty 等 (2013)；George (2010)
组合构建中的复制不变性；针对模型空间冗余进行校正的稀释先验（dilution prior）。
实证度量经调参程序偏离这种不变性的程度，从主题一直到具体股票。


Ke and Pourmohammadi (2025)
按各资产夏普比率设定收缩强度（夏普比率收缩），在资产盈利能力不同时可改进高维组合。
以该规则的改编版作为四种方法之一，并表明它同样对表示方式敏感：季节性主题复制五份，使其 25 个基点下的平均收益下降 1.30 个百分点（第 III.D 节）。


Kelly 等 (2024)
更丰富、更复杂的模型可以改进收益预测；Nagel (2025) 对其普遍性提出质疑。
研究的是不增加新函数的精确复制；本文不检验更广泛的复杂性论点。




本文的切入点是实证性的，范围有意收窄。对照所依据的恒等式早已为人所知；新意在于在同一面板上度量四种经调参程序的反应大小，并把反应追踪到个股头寸和依赖成本的收益（引言）。由此得到一套管理人在采用特征库更新前可以执行的诊断：在既定实施方式下，检查拟合的主题归因、个股目标持仓和净收益。主题再平衡只是一个透明的备选加权方式，并非“正确”的加权。作者的两篇配套论文分别研究组合选择中的特征几何（《特征几何与投资组合选择》）和因子模型中的特征空间度量与识别（《因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断》）。

text:
8 适用范围

文章不主张可投资的业绩。成本不含融券费用和市场冲击；在基于买卖价差的成本代理下，三种 UPSA 版本的平均收益均为负（第 IV.C 节）。收益还取决于缺失收益如何估值：在扣费前的情形下，原始 UPSA 在主要估值口径下的平均收益为 4.79%；若把收益缺失的头寸按 +100% 或 −100% 总收益估值，则在 0.62% 到 8.98% 之间。这些只是情景，并非上下界（第 IV.C 节）。
文章不给出最优特征库，也不证明主题再平衡更好。
文章并不认为新增特征缺乏信息；预测效应小且不确定，这一结论只针对这些估计程序本身（第 V.A 节；第 VII 节）。
数据是回溯提取的美国样本，研究设计也是在这份数据上形成的，且未经预注册（第 II.F 节；第 VI.D 节）。
区间以已拟合的决策为条件；区间包含零并不等于二者等价（第 VI.A 节）。

title: Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts
text:
1 The question
When a model reports a smaller estimated pricing error, what has changed, and can the estimate help a user choose or improve a return forecast?
A pricing error, or alpha, is the part of a stock’s expected return that a factor benchmark does not explain (Section 2.1, equation 1). Both the expected return and the factors are estimated, so a reported alpha can shrink because the factors explain more or because the expected return itself changed. The paper separates the two, then asks whether alpha size helps select a forecast and whether the alpha component is useful inside one.

title: Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts
text:
2 Why it matters
Smaller estimated alphas are a common argument for a new model. If the gap mostly reflects a different fitted mean, the argument is about the signal, not the factors.

Economic. An alpha is relative to a benchmark, an information set and a horizon. Comparing two estimates without holding the explained signal fixed compares two different objects.
Practical. Teams choose between forecasts and decide how much of a model’s alpha component to keep. Both decisions can be tested on later returns.
Statistical. An estimated alpha is noisy. Keeping all of it can add error; dropping it can lose signal. Only a matched out-of-sample comparison says which dominates.

title: Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts
text:
3 The argument at a glance


Question. A smaller estimated alpha can mean better factors or a different fitted mean; which is it? → The question
Why it matters. Model comparison, forecast choice and alpha use all depend on reading this number correctly. → Why it matters
Framework. Split each fitted mean into a factor part and a characteristic-intercept part, measured on the same stocks with the same weights. → The framework
Mechanism. Cross two fitted means with two loading spaces. Swapping the space barely moves the residual; swapping the mean moves it a lot. → A simple example; Table 1
Evidence. Selecting forecasts by residual size adds little (Section 5.1). Keeping a fitted fraction of the intercept part beats the complete forecast in 20 of 24 specifications, but the equal forecast average in only 8 and characteristic-PC calibration in only 6 (Table G.1). → Figure 3
Contribution. One matched design that separates three questions: explaining an alpha, selecting with it, and using it. → How it relates to prior work
Boundary. Exploratory evidence on clipped next-month returns; not a pricing-error test and not a trading result. → Scope

title: Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts
text:
4 The framework
For a set of stocks at date t, with expected excess returns \mu_t, factor exposures \beta_t and risk prices \lambda_t, the pricing error is

\alpha_t = \mu_t - \beta_t \lambda_t .

It is in monthly return units (equation 1), and it is not realised noise or proof of mispricing.
The empirical model is a characteristic-based latent-factor model in the style of instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA) (Kelly et al. 2019). Stock characteristics generate both factor exposures, through a loading matrix B, and an intercept (equation 2). The model’s fitted mean coefficient \hat h splits into a factor part p and a characteristic-intercept part r:

\begin{aligned}
\hat h &= \underbrace{P_Q(B)\,\hat h}_{p:\ \text{factor part}} + \underbrace{[I - P_Q(B)]\,\hat h}_{r:\ \text{intercept part}},\\
h(\eta) &= p + \eta\, r,\qquad \eta \in [0,1].
\end{aligned}

P_Q(B) projects onto the loading space: every return signal the model’s exposures can produce. Q, a characteristic Gram matrix, measures coefficient differences by how differently they forecast the stocks studied, under equal-stock (EW) or capitalisation (VW) weights (Section 2.2, equations 3 to 5). Under a stated factor-location convention (how the factors’ mean is set), r is exactly the model’s fitted characteristic alpha (Section 2.3, equation 6). When a space is asked to explain another model’s mean, the leftover is a projection residual, not an alpha.
The second half of the display is the forecast-use decision: keep the factor part and a fraction \eta of the intercept part (equation 14). At \eta = 1 the forecast is complete; at \eta = 0 only the factor part is left. Choosing \eta from past forecast errors is what the paper calls residual calibration. Here “residual” means the model’s own intercept part r, not a cross-model projection residual. For the wider characteristic-geometry line, see Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models (Liu 2026) and A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models.

The data are the U.S. stock panel associated with the characteristic library of Jensen et al. (2023): 153 characteristics and 749 formation months, July 1963 to November 2025. The target is the next month’s excess return, clipped at the monthly 1st and 99th percentiles (Section 3.1). Forecasts are issued at nine annual origins, March 2017 to March 2025, for 105 target months, April 2017 to December 2025. Training outcomes always precede forecast outcomes (Section 3.2). section: 7 How it relates to prior work
text:
7 How it relates to prior work
The paper builds on characteristic-based factor models and recent work on their pricing errors, and borrows yardsticks from return prediction and forecast combination.









Prior work
What it established
What this paper adds




Kelly et al. (2019)
Characteristics instrument for factor loadings; an intercept captures characteristic-linked return not due to factor exposure.
Uses this setting and asks what a change in the fitted intercept’s size actually reflects.


Zhang (2024)
Specification and tests of pricing errors with latent factors and characteristics as covariances.
Not a new test; a matched comparison of fitted objects and their forecast use.


Choi and Yuan (2025)
Estimation and inference for “inside” and “outside” alphas, with debiasing.
A different question: what a reported fall in a fitted alpha changes. The paper does not rank itself against these estimators.


Kim et al. (2021)
Attribute characteristic-predicted returns to factor loadings first, and form arbitrage portfolios from the remainder orthogonal to the loadings.
Asks a forecasting version: how much of a model’s characteristic-intercept component to keep in an issued return forecast, judged against simple controls and without a portfolio claim.


Kozak et al. (2020)
A shrinkage prior on a stochastic discount factor over many characteristic portfolios performs well out of sample; a few principal components summarise it better than a few characteristics.
Uses ridge as a prediction benchmark and treats partial retention of the alpha component as a separate, testable shrinkage decision.


Pástor and Stambaugh (2000)
Compares pricing models by their investment consequences.
Compares them by forecast decisions on a common task, without a portfolio claim.


Bates and Granger (1969)
Combined forecasts can beat each component under squared loss.
Shows why equal averaging is a demanding control for selection and calibration rules.




The identities that make the objects comparable are shared with the author’s companion work (Liu 2026). The contribution here is empirical: one design, on the same stocks, dates and loss, separates three questions that a residual comparison tends to blur: what explains an estimated alpha’s size, whether the size helps select a forecast, and whether the component helps inside one. The answers are: mostly the mean; little; sometimes. The paper reports the unfavourable cells and the window reversals alongside the favourable ones.

title: Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts
text:
8 Scope

Not a pricing-error test. The comparisons do not test whether population alphas are zero (Appendix I.2).
Not a trading result. The target is a clipped next-month excess return; prediction R^2 is not a portfolio return, and no costs or constraints are modelled (Appendix I.3).
Not independent evidence. Nine annual choices and 24 overlapping specifications are sensitivity summaries, not independent replications or confidence intervals (Section 3.4; Appendix I.2).
Not about all alphas. The object is the characteristic intercept under a stated convention, not every stock-level pricing error.
Exploratory history. The sample informed the design, and the source return vintage is not fully reconciled (Section 3.2; Appendix I.3).

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
1 The question
When firm characteristics are correlated and unevenly scaled, which combinations of them form the priced span of a factor model, and which are only redundant or residual?
Expected returns are now linked to dozens of characteristics at once. Principal component analysis (PCA), instrumented PCA (IPCA) (Kelly et al. 2019) and many machine-learning estimators measure length and orthogonality in characteristic space with the identity matrix (paper, Section 1.1). That choice is seldom stated. The paper makes it explicit and asks what changes when the ruler comes from the data.

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
2 Why it matters
The ruler decides what counts as “different”. Under the plain ruler, two loading vectors can be perpendicular and still pick the same stocks. An estimator can then split one priced direction into two factors, or let a latent factor copy an observed benchmark factor already in the model (paper, Section 1.1).

Economic. Which directions earn a risk premium, and how much pricing is left to the intercept, both depend on the ruler used to tell directions apart (paper, Section 1.1).
Practical. A user who reads a latent factor as a new risk may be holding a benchmark exposure twice.
Statistical. In-sample fit does not reveal the problem. In the paper’s simulations, IPCA fits returns with an R² between 0.94 and 0.99 even when its latent span is far from the true one (paper, Section 7.3; Table 9).

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
3 The argument at a glance


Question. Which combinations of characteristics are priced once their correlation and scale are taken seriously? → The question
Why. A plain ruler lets one priced direction be split, duplicated or absorbed by the intercept. → Why it matters
Framework. Measure directions with the long-run characteristic metric, and write the normalisation, block separation and a no-arbitrage bound in that metric; the resulting estimator is No-Arbitrage IPCA (NA-IPCA). → The framework
Mechanism. Directions that look perpendicular under the plain ruler can overlap under the data’s ruler, so separating blocks in that ruler stops double counting. → A simple example
Evidence. The U.S. characteristic metric is strongly uneven. In simulations calibrated to it, where the priced directions follow the characteristic metric, NA-IPCA recovers the latent span; IPCA without an intercept block and PCA do not. → Design and main results
Contribution. The metric becomes an explicit object of identification, and IPCA is the special case of a flat ruler with no bound. → How it relates to prior work
Boundary. The evidence concerns characteristic geometry and simulations; a full asset-pricing application is left to companion work. → Scope

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
4 The framework
Let Z_t hold L characteristics for the N_t stocks observed in month t. The paper’s ruler is the long-run characteristic metric (paper, Section 2):

Q_Z = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{1}{N_t} Z_t^{\top} Z_t .

It is the long-run average of the characteristic Gram matrix: how characteristics move together across stocks. Under this ruler the length of a coefficient vector a is (a^{\top} Q_Z a)^{1/2}: roughly, how widely the exposures it creates vary across stocks. Two directions are orthogonal when the characteristic portfolios they create do not co-move in the long run (paper, Section 2).
Expected excess returns are split into three blocks (paper, Section 2):

\mathbb{E}_t\!\left[r_{t+1}\right] = Z_t\left(\Gamma_\beta f_t + \Gamma_\delta F^{\text{obs}}_t + \Gamma_\alpha\right).

\Gamma_\beta loads on latent factors f_t. \Gamma_\delta loads on observed factors, such as traded benchmark factors. \Gamma_\alpha is a characteristic-driven intercept (paper, Table 1). All restrictions are written in Q_Z: the latent loadings are orthonormal (\Gamma_\beta^{\top} Q_Z \Gamma_\beta = I), the observed and intercept blocks are orthogonal to the latent span, and the intercept’s size \Gamma_\alpha^{\top} Q_Z \Gamma_\alpha is capped by a bound \delta. A small \delta approaches strict no-arbitrage (paper, Section 2).
The estimator, No-Arbitrage IPCA (NA-IPCA), is weighted least squares restricted to this set; its solution is characterised by weighted least-squares equations projected onto the tangent space of that set (paper, Proposition 3.1). With a flat ruler and no bound, it reduces to statistical IPCA (paper, Section 8). The paper also derives rotation-invariant asymptotic inference for the identified spans under stated conditions (paper, Section 4).

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
6 Design and main results
The paper first estimates Q_Z on the replication panel of Kelly et al. (2019): 37 rank-transformed characteristics including a constant, 12,813 firms and 599 months from July 1964 to May 2014 (paper, Section 6.1; Table 2). It then simulates 1,000 stocks over 240 months with characteristics drawn to match this metric. The design has three latent factors on the leading directions of Q_Z and two deliberately weak observed factors (paper, Section 7.1; Table 7). It compares NA-IPCA, IPCA without an intercept block, and PCA over 300 replications (paper, footnote 11).


Figure 2: The characteristic ruler is far from round. Variance share of the first 15 principal components of Q_Z.



How to read it. Each bar is one principal direction of the characteristic metric. A round ruler would give every one of the 37 directions about 3 percent. Source: SSRN preprint, March 2026, Figure 2, p. 33 (reproduced from the paper). Paper page



What this shows. The first principal component carries 25 percent of characteristic dispersion and the first five carry 62 percent; a flat ruler would give each about 3 percent (paper, Section 6.2; Table 5). Eigenvalues range from 0.002 to 1.0, a condition number of 502 (paper, Table 2). Many raw characteristics are versions of a few traits: size, value, profitability, investment and momentum form tight clusters (paper, Section 6.2). Statistically, a plain ruler gives nearly redundant combinations the same weight as the directions along which firms truly differ. The paper reads these few high-dispersion directions as the ones with the most scope to support risk compensation (paper, Section 1.1); the geometry alone does not show which directions are priced.



Figure 3: When priced directions follow the characteristic metric, NA-IPCA recovers the latent span; IPCA and PCA do not. Distance between estimated and true loading spans, geometry-calibrated simulation.



How to read it. The distance is \lVert \sin\Theta \rVert_F, built from the angles between the estimated and the true span. It is 0 for exact recovery. Its maximum, reached when the estimated span is orthogonal to the true one, is \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73 for the three latent directions and \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41 for the two observed directions (paper, footnote 10). Lower is better. Source: SSRN preprint, March 2026, Figure 4, p. 39, and Table 8, p. 38 (reproduced from the paper). Paper page



What this shows. For the latent span, the distance is 0.011 for NA-IPCA, 0.73 for IPCA and 0.99 for PCA (paper, Table 8). IPCA also lets its latent and observed blocks overlap: 0.069 against 0.0005 for NA-IPCA (paper, Table 8). That is the double counting of the toy example, reproduced in a simulated panel of 37 characteristics calibrated to U.S. data. On the observed block the ranking reverses: IPCA’s distance is 0.23 and NA-IPCA’s is 1.40, close to the maximum of 1.41 for two directions (paper, Table 8). The paper reads this as NA-IPCA declining to price observed factors that were made deliberately weak (paper, Section 7.2).

In this design the true loadings are the leading eigenvectors of the empirical Q_Z in every row, and only the sampling law of the characteristics changes (paper, Sections 7.1, 7.3). title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
section: 7 How it relates to prior work
text:
7 How it relates to prior work
The paper sits where three literatures meet: large-panel factor models, economic discipline on factors, and shrinkage or machine-learning estimators of the stochastic discount factor (paper, Section 1.2). Each has sharpened what a factor model can identify. The table lists the closest reference points.









Prior work
What it established
What this paper adds




Approximate factor models (Bai and Ng 2002)
How many common factors a large panel has, under weak dependence
Once the number is set, asks which directions form the priced span, measured with an estimated metric


IPCA (Kelly et al. 2019)
Characteristics instrument time-varying betas; the same model admits a characteristic-driven intercept and observable factors, and tests whether each is zero
Writes the normalisation and the separation of the latent, observed and intercept blocks in Q_Z, and caps the intercept; IPCA, with its Euclidean normalisation and no cap, is the flat, unbounded case


RP-PCA (Lettau and Pelger 2020)
Adding a pricing-error penalty to PCA gives factors that also fit average returns
Places pricing discipline in the feasible set, through the metric and an intercept bound


Weak and spurious factors (Bryzgalova 2015)
Factors with weak covariance can look spuriously significant and crowd out true risks
Carries the weak-factor concern into characteristic space: argues that a plain ruler lets weak, redundant directions absorb variation, and builds weak observed factors into its simulations


Near-arbitrage bounds (Kozak et al. 2018)
Absent near-arbitrage, the SDF is well approximated by a few high-variance principal components
Imposes a related bound directly on the intercept block, in the characteristic metric


Shrinking the cross-section (Kozak et al. 2020)
A prior that shrinks SDF coefficients on characteristic portfolios, most strongly along their low-variance principal components
Uses the characteristic metric not as a penalty but to define the model’s normalisation and the separation of its blocks


Volatility bounds (Hansen and Jagannathan 1991)
Asset prices bound the volatility of any valid SDF
Motivates a quadratic cap, in the same metric, on the pricing content of the intercept block




The angle is the ruler. Much prior work imposes pricing restrictions on top of a factor extraction whose geometry is already fixed (paper, Section 1.2). This paper makes the characteristic metric an explicit, estimated object. It writes normalisation, block separation and a residual bound in that metric, and gives an estimator and inference for the result. The evidence supports a specific claim, not a general ranking of methods: when characteristics are uneven and correlated, the choice of ruler changes which directions a model identifies. The later paper Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference develops the identification and inference part with an estimated metric.

title: A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models
text:
8 Scope

The paper does not show that NA-IPCA forecasts returns or builds portfolios better. Its evidence is the geometry of characteristic space and calibrated simulations; a full asset-pricing application is left to a companion study (paper, Section 8).
In the simulations the true latent loadings sit on the leading directions of Q_Z (paper, Section 7.1). The results show what goes wrong when a plain ruler meets such a geometry, not that every market has it.
The IPCA benchmark in the simulations is the restricted version with no intercept block, while the simulated returns contain one (paper, Sections 7.1-7.2). The comparison is therefore not a test of the ruler alone.
Q_Z is an estimated description of one sample, 1964 to 2014. If the distribution of characteristics shifts, it should be re-estimated (paper, Section 8).
The asymptotic results hold under stated regularity, identification and centring conditions (paper, Section 4). This page does not present them as a general efficiency result or as local asymptotic normality in Le Cam’s sense.
The intercept block is a bounded residual component of the model. It is not a measured mispricing or an alpha.

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
text:
1 The question
When a characteristic library changes without gaining information, does a tuned investment rule still change, and does the change reach holdings and net returns?
Repeating a column adds no observation and leaves the set of reachable linear portfolios unchanged. But a regularized estimator charges a penalty per coefficient, so copies make a theme cheaper to use, even after the penalty is tuned again (Introduction; Section I.B). The paper measures how large this effect is for four tuned portfolio methods. It follows the effect from the estimated weights to economic themes, named stocks and returns after costs.

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
text:
2 Why it matters
Managers update these libraries routinely (Introduction). The widely used Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen library has 153 characteristics in 13 themes (Section II.A), and overlap within themes is uneven. Quality has 17 columns but a correlation participation rank of only 3.47, a rough count of distinct directions in the data (not of independent information sources); seasonality has 12 columns and a rank of 11.78 (paper, Section III.A; Table II). If a better backtest can come from how inputs are written down rather than from what they measure, then a library update needs a different kind of check.

Economic. A manager may read a new tilt toward, say, value as new evidence about value. Part of it can be a bookkeeping effect of the library.
Practical. Tilts become trades. Trades cost money, so a change in representation can change net returns even when gross returns barely move.
Statistical. A lower test error does not prove that new inputs carry new information. A tuned rule can improve because its penalty changed.

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
text:
3 The argument at a glance


Question. Does an information-preserving change to the library change a tuned investment rule? → The question
Why. Library updates are routine, and their value is usually judged by backtests that cannot separate information from reweighting. → Why it matters
Framework. Exact copies and theme rescaling keep the data and the reachable portfolios fixed, so any response belongs to the fitted procedure. → The framework
Mechanism. Copying a theme divides its effective ridge penalty by the number of copies, which tilts the fit toward that theme. → A simple example

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
text:
4 The framework
The design holds the investment method, the eligible stocks and the decision dates fixed and changes only the library (Introduction). Two controlled changes carry no new information. Selective copies give every column of one theme five total copies. Theme balancing rescales each theme’s columns by its column count, so a theme with many columns no longer gets more room under the penalty than a theme with few. The mechanism is one line of algebra. If a characteristic is replaced by m identical columns with coefficients \theta_j that add up to b, the cheapest way to split b gives

\min_{\sum_j \theta_j = b} \; \sum_{j=1}^{m} \theta_j^2 \;=\; \frac{b^2}{m}.

So a ridge penalty on the copies charges only 1/m of the usual price for the same exposure (Section I.B, equation 2). For stock ridge there is an exact control: scale the copies’ penalty back up (“transport” it) and the original problem returns (Section I.B).
Every estimate is then mapped back to the 153 original characteristics and scored in the same 13 themes (Section III.B). A theme’s weight is its share of the fitted payoff’s variance,

s_g = \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(u_g, u)}{\operatorname{Var}(u)},

where u_g is theme g’s payoff and u the total. The shares add up to one and can be negative when a theme hedges (Section I.D, equation 4). The change in attribution is half the sum of absolute share changes. The paper compares it with the change in stock targets and in returns after costs, because each measures a different consequence.

6 Design and main results
The library is the Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen database of 153 U.S. characteristics in 13 themes (Jensen et al. 2023), extracted in May 2026 (Section II.A). There are 179 monthly decisions from January 2011 to November 2025, each estimated on the previous 120 months, with returns through December 2025 (Section II.C). The four methods are blocked ridge, a training-Sharpe-weighted ridge (SR-weighted) adapted from Ke and Pourmohammadi (2025), Universal Portfolio Shrinkage (UPSA) (Kelly et al. 2026), and the leave-one-out (LOO) ridge inside UPSA’s code (Section III.B). One allocation rule turns every estimate into stock positions: a 10% volatility target and a gross exposure cap of two. Stock-level ledgers then charge costs of 10 to 100 basis points per traded dollar (Sections IV.A and IV.C).

The vertical axis is annual arithmetic mean excess return in percent. Each rate has a separate self-financing cash and return-drift account; target-weight rules remain fixed. The stock gross cap is two and primary missing outcomes receive zero vendor excess return. The curves do not include optimized trade scheduling, borrow fees or market impact.” (paper, Figure 3) Before costs, LOO ridge and UPSA earn about 4.5% to 5.1% a year (paper, Table IV). At 25 basis points, balancing lowers UPSA’s mean to 0.92%, a difference of −0.19 points whose 95% interval, [−0.57, 0.19], includes zero; five seasonality copies cut the SR-weighted ridge’s mean by 1.30 points, with a band of [−2.35, −0.25] that holds jointly across its 13 copy experiments (Section III.D). Source: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions, Figure 3 and Table IV; results file summary.csv. Data



What this shows. Trading costs take most of the gross return. All four original books trade 1.13 to 1.28 dollars per dollar of capital a month (paper, Table V), so at 25 basis points original UPSA’s mean falls from 4.79% to 1.10% a year (paper, Section IV.C; Table IV). Library changes then shift net returns by amounts that are mostly within sampling error; the caption gives the one clearly adverse case.

The paper then asks the opposite question: what do real new characteristics add? Growing monthly ridge from 39 to 153 characteristics raises normalized prediction loss, measured relative to the loss of a zero forecast, by 0.0079 percentage points. That is a slight deterioration, but the 95% interval of [−0.040, 0.068] allows both gains and losses (Section V.A). The plain historical mean does slightly better than either library: out-of-sample R² of 0.239%, against 0.214% with 39 characteristics and 0.206% with 153 (paper, Section V.A; Table VI).


Figure 3: Leaving out one theme at a time. Paper Figure 4.



How to read it. Each row drops one theme from the full library and refits the ridge forecast. Points to the right of zero mean the forecast got worse without that theme. Dark bars are pointwise 95% intervals; light bands hold jointly across all 13 themes. Figure note from the paper: “An omission removes shared and distinct content together.” (paper, Figure 4) Source: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions, Figure 4 (p. 34 of the PDF).



What this shows. No single theme is reliably needed for the forecast. Dropping quality has the largest point estimate, raising loss by about 0.026 points, yet every simultaneous band includes zero (paper, Section V.A; Figure 4). That does not mean the themes carry no information. It means this procedure, on this sample, extracts too little to measure precisely. Real additions and the copy controls answer different questions, and the paper keeps them apart.

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
section: 7 How it relates to prior work
text:
7 How it relates to prior work
Shrinkage and regularization are now standard tools for building portfolios from many characteristics. The closest studies compare methods on a given library. This paper holds each method fixed and changes only how the library is written down.









Prior work
What it established
What this paper adds




Kozak et al. (2020)
Shrinkage of characteristic-portfolio weights gives robust out-of-sample stochastic discount factors.
Shows that the same kind of penalty responds to how the library is represented, and traces that response into holdings.


Kelly et al. (2026)
UPSA combines ridge portfolios to target out-of-sample performance and groups weights into economic themes.
Keeps UPSA’s public code fixed and changes its inputs; balancing shifts UPSA’s theme shares by a distance of 0.274 (paper, Table I).


Jensen et al. (2023)
Builds a public library of 153 factors in 13 themes and finds that most factors replicate, including out of sample and across 93 countries.
Uses that library as the object of study: its uneven within-theme overlap motivates the controls.


Jensen et al. (2026)
Portfolios should be judged net of trading costs; cost-aware learning improves the implementable frontier.
Uses a fixed, non-optimized allocation rule and explicit cost ledgers to show that library changes reach net returns; a cost-aware optimizer like theirs could change the response (Section IV.A).


Choueifaty et al. (2013); George (2010)
Duplication invariance in portfolio construction; priors that correct for redundant models.
Supplies an empirical measure of how far tuned procedures depart from such invariance, from themes to named stocks.


Ke and Pourmohammadi (2025)
Setting each asset’s shrinkage strength by its Sharpe ratio (Sharpe Ratio Shrinkage) can improve high-dimensional portfolios when profitability differs across assets.
Uses an adaptation of this rule as one of the four methods and shows that it too responds to representation: five seasonality copies lower its 25 bp mean by 1.30 points (Section III.D).


Kelly et al. (2024)
Richer, more complex models can improve return prediction; Nagel (2025) questions how general this is.
Studies exact copies, which add no new function; the paper does not test the broader complexity argument.




The angle is empirical and narrow on purpose. The identities behind the controls are known. What is new is measuring how much four tuned procedures respond on a common panel, and following the response to stock positions and cost-dependent returns (Introduction). The result is a diagnostic a manager can run before adopting a library update: check the fitted attribution, the stock targets and the net payoff under the chosen implementation. Theme balancing is offered as a transparent alternative weighting, not as the right one. Companion papers study characteristic geometry in portfolio choice (Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice) and metric-based identification in factor models (Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models).

title: Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions
text:
8 Scope

The paper makes no claim of investable performance. Costs exclude borrow fees and market impact, and under a spread-based cost proxy all three UPSA versions have negative means (Section IV.C). Returns also depend on how missing returns are valued: before fees, original UPSA’s mean is 4.79% under the primary valuation but ranges from 0.62% to 8.98% when positions with unobserved returns are valued at +100% or −100% total return. These are scenarios, not bounds (Section IV.C).
It does not identify an optimal library, and it does not show that theme balancing is better.
It does not claim that the added characteristics lack information. Small, uncertain forecast effects describe these procedures only (Section V.A; Section VII).
The data are a retrospective U.S. extraction that was also used to develop the design, which was not preregistered (Section II.F; Section VI.D).
Intervals condition on the fitted decisions, and an interval that contains zero does not establish equivalence (Section VI.A).

title: Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice
text:
1 The question
When a factor model’s forecast is turned into a portfolio, how do the units used to measure characteristic exposures change what the investor holds?
Characteristic-based factor models such as IPCA (Kelly et al. 2019) let a stock’s factor exposures depend on its traits, such as size or book-to-market. The model must fix what one unit of exposure means and when two exposures count as unrelated. The paper calls this choice the metric, or more simply the ruler. It leaves fitted returns unchanged. Does it change the portfolio? And what does keeping a fitted intercept in expected returns add?

title: Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice
text:
2 Why it matters
Research usually compares factor models by their forecasts, but investors hold portfolios. Forecasts become positions through a risk model with its own units and regularisation. If those conventions move holdings, a change in holdings can be mistaken for news.

Economic. Forecasts that agree to about five parts in a million still give portfolios whose median weight cosine is 0.83, where 1 means the same direction (Slides 9). That gap does not come from different forecasts.
Practical. A change in how a risk model measures or regularises factor exposure can move positions with no new forecast. Knowing the channel tells a manager what to hold fixed.
Statistical. Characteristic libraries are crowded. Across 618 months, the 132 characteristics vary like about 20 equally important directions: the median participation dimension is 19.8 (Slides 7). So how their overlap is measured is a real modelling choice.
Investment value of the intercept. A factor-only portfolio drops the fitted intercept. Measuring that input’s worth within one fit separates it from the value of a better model.

title: Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice
text:
4 The framework
The model writes each stock’s next-month excess return as its characteristics times three blocks of coefficients: latent factors, the five Fama-French factors, and an intercept that does not move with any factor (Slides 4):

r_{i,s+1} = z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\beta f_{s+1} + z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\delta g_{s+1} + z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\alpha + \varepsilon_{i,s+1}.

Here z_{i,s} lists stock i’s characteristics, f are three latent factors, g the observed factors, and each \Gamma turns characteristics into loadings. The data pin down only the sum of the three blocks; the ruler decides how it is split. IPCA uses the plain ruler, which treats every characteristic as its own, equally scaled axis. QZ-IPCA uses the characteristic Gram matrix, the average across stocks of products of characteristics. Under it, two loading directions count as unrelated only if the stock exposures they generate have a zero average cross-product (Slides 5, 6).
The paper builds this Gram matrix in three ways inside each 120-month window: an exponentially weighted average with a 60-month half-life (EWMA), an equal-weight average of all 120 months, and an average of the last 60 months (rolling 60) (Slides A14). The EWMA ruler is the one used for the mechanism checks; Figure 3 shows the rolling-60 ruler. NA-IPCA adds a fitted intercept under a size budget of 0.035 that never binds in this sample (Slides 13, A2).
Switching rulers is a matched change of units: loadings are rescaled, overlap moves between blocks, the factor series compensates, and every fitted return and residual is unchanged (Slides 6, A13). The general theory is in the companion paper (Liu 2026).
Every model feeds the same mean-variance rule, with a ridge of 0.01 added to each factor variance and each stock variance for numerical stability (Slides 8). Written out, the rule chooses weights w to solve (Slides 8, 10)

\max_w \; w'\hat\mu \;-\; \tfrac12\, w'A_0\, w \;-\; \tfrac{\lambda_F}{2}\,\lVert B'w\rVert^2 ,

where \hat\mu is the forecast, A_0 is the risk matrix without the factor ridge, B'w is the portfolio’s exposure to each factor and \lambda_F = 0.01. When the forecast and the factor covariance are transformed together with the loadings, the first two terms survive a change of ruler exactly (Slides A13). The last term charges factor exposure in each factor’s own units, so it does not (Slides 10). Positions are then scaled so that long plus short equals one dollar (Slides 8).

section: 7 How it relates to prior work
text:
7 How it relates to prior work
One literature builds forecasts and factors from many characteristics; another shrinks or constrains risk estimates in stock space. This paper studies the step between them, where a factor model’s output passes through a regularised risk model and becomes a portfolio.









Prior work
What it established
What this paper adds




Kelly et al. (2019)
Characteristics instrument time-varying factor loadings (IPCA). Return the factors miss goes to an anomaly intercept, and with five factors those intercepts are small and statistically insignificant
Shows that the loading normalisation, harmless for fit, changes portfolios through a fixed factor ridge. For the intercept, it measures the gross portfolio value of a bounded intercept within one fit (three latent factors plus FF5); it does not re-test their zero-intercept restriction


Gu et al. (2020)
Machine-learning forecasts from many characteristics create large gains for investors
Holds forecasts almost fixed and shows that the portfolio can still change with the risk model’s regulariser, so forecast agreement does not imply portfolio agreement


Lettau and Pelger (2020)
Adding a mean-fit penalty to PCA recovers factors that matter for expected returns (RP-PCA)
Uses RP-PCA as a benchmark under the same rule; varies how a model’s output is used, not the estimator


Jagannathan and Ma (2003)
Portfolio weight constraints act like covariance shrinkage
A ridge on factor variances acts like a stock-level exposure penalty whose form depends on factor units


Ledoit and Wolf (2017)
Nonlinear covariance shrinkage improves portfolio selection
A factor-space regulariser keeps its meaning only if it is transported with the coordinates or written in stock space


Zaffaroni (2025)
In conditional factor models with large cross-sections, asymptotic no-arbitrage implies pricing errors that are small in aggregate (square-summable), not zero intercepts, and omitted factors complicate reading alpha
Bounds the intercept’s exposure and measures its portfolio value, without claiming it is mispricing


Brandt et al. (2009)
Portfolio weights can be modelled directly as functions of characteristics, with no covariance matrix
Here the portfolio passes through a factor model and a factor covariance. That is where the factor-ridge channel enters, and it has nowhere to enter in their design




The contribution is narrow. First, an algebraic observation: a normalisation that leaves the fit unchanged enters the portfolio through a fixed factor ridge, and the remedy is to transport the ridge or write it in stock space. Second, a stored-matrix experiment that confirms this channel in each of 618 months (Slides 11, A10). Third, a same-fit ablation that measures the gross value of the retained intercept. It is a check for factor-based portfolio rules, not a new estimator.

title: Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice
text:
8 Scope

Gross is not net. All Sharpe ratios are before trading, financing and borrowing costs, under unit-gross scaling; the cost lines in Figure 3 are a proxy (Slides 8, A30).
Ridge removal is a mechanism check, not a performance test. Returns of ridge-free or transported-ridge portfolios were not computed (Slides 11, A13).
Overlap is not a count of priced risks. The Gram matrix and its participation dimension measure how much characteristic exposures overlap, not how many risks are priced (Slides 5, 7).
The intercept is not shown to be mispricing or arbitrage. Its positions can carry factor exposure, and a pricing reading needs a specified factor-pricing benchmark. The weaker recent results do not establish a structural change (Slides 15, A32).
No best ruler is established. Three Gram constructions are reported, none is chosen by significance, and the intervals are pointwise without adjustment for the number of comparisons (Slides A15 to A17).

title: Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference
text:
1 The question
When a characteristic-based factor model fits returns, what decides how the fit is divided among latent factors, observed factors and the intercept, and how precisely can that division be measured?
Models in the IPCA (instrumented principal component analysis) family let firm characteristics such as size, value and momentum set each stock’s factor loadings. When latent factors sit next to observed factors and an intercept, a change in the latent factors can offset a reallocation of loadings across blocks, leaving every fitted return unchanged (Section 1). Many characteristics also overlap: two value signals often pick out the same stocks. That overlap is what makes the choice of rule consequential.

title: Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference
text:
2 Why it matters
Researchers routinely report how much a latent block loads on a benchmark, how large a residual intercept is, or which characteristic directions the latent factors span. Each of these numbers depends on the allocation, not only on the fit.

Economic. A benchmark exposure or an intercept can look large under one ruler and small under another, with identical fitted returns (Proposition 1).
Practical. Residual sums of squares and R² cannot decide between rulers, because they depend only on the fitted values (Corollary 1).
Statistical. The paper’s ruler, the average Gram matrix of characteristics, is itself estimated from the data. Treating it as known drops the metric’s variance and its covariance with the return score (Theorem 1); in the paper’s simulations this makes standard errors too small (Section 8.2).

title: Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference
text:
3 The argument at a glance


Question. Which rule divides one fitted return among latent, observed-factor and intercept blocks? → The question
Stakes. Reported exposures change with that rule while fit does not, so fit statistics cannot choose it. → Why it matters
Framework. An inner product on characteristic space, the metric, picks the division; changing it re-splits the fit without changing any fitted return. → The framework
Mechanism. Changing the metric moves fitted return between blocks while the total stays fixed. The metric is estimated from the same panel, so its error enters the reported exposures and can move an exposure limit. → A simple example
Evidence. Real characteristics leave a nontrivial set of overlapping exposures and a concentrated spectrum; in simulations, ignoring metric error lowers coverage; near a learned limit, drift-robust intervals keep coverage. → Design and main results
Contribution. A standard-error formula that counts the error in the estimated ruler and does not depend on how the model is parameterized, plus a confidence interval that stays valid near an exposure limit whether or not the limit binds. → How it relates to prior work
Boundary. The theory is local, assumes the model is strongly identified near one solution, and covers smooth reported quantities. → Scope

title: Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference
text:
4 The framework
At each date, stock i has characteristics z_{i,t} and a next-period excess return. The model has three blocks (equation 2.1):

r_{i,t+1} = z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\beta f_{t+1} + z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\delta g_{t+1} + z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\alpha + \varepsilon_{i,t+1}.

Here f are latent factors, g are observed factors and \Gamma_\alpha is a characteristic-driven intercept. To separate the blocks, the model needs a notion of when two loading directions overlap. The Gram metric measures overlap by the stock exposures the directions generate (equation 2.5):

\langle a,b\rangle_{Q_Z} = a'Q_Z\,b = \mathbb{E}\!\left[N_t^{-1}(Z_t a)'(Z_t b)\right].

Two coefficient vectors can be perpendicular on paper and still buy the same stocks. Under this ruler they overlap.
The theory has three steps.

Identification. For any positive-definite metric, a matched transformation normalizes the latent loadings, removes the other blocks’ overlap with them, and offsets both changes in the factor series. Every fitted return is unchanged (Proposition 1). The object of inference is therefore a loading class with latent rotations removed. Local curvature of the population criterion identifies it (Proposition 2). A covariance-alignment condition is sufficient, together with local regularity, for this target to be the structural loading class even with a fixed cross section (Proposition 3).
Inference with a learned metric. The estimator is exactly profiled: given the loadings, each date’s factors are solved by least squares with fixed date weights. On a regular local branch (near one well-behaved solution), its large-sample expansion adds a metric-estimation term to the usual return term, including their covariance (Theorem 1). Smooth reports, such as alignment with a characteristic direction, distance from a benchmark span, or intercept exposure, inherit one influence function. An influence function says how much each date’s data move the estimate; here it gives a formula for sampling error that does not depend on how the model is parameterized (Theorem 2). A standard HAC (heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent) estimator of it gives asymptotically valid intervals (Proposition 5).
A learned exposure limit. A budget can cap intercept exposure. Near that cap, the estimated metric moves the feasible boundary as well as the score, so the sampling law is a projection, not a symmetric normal (Theorem 3). Intervals built from least-favorable quantiles (critical values taken at whichever amount of unknown slack is hardest for coverage) have at least nominal coverage asymptotically, uniformly over unknown slack, and may be conservative (Theorem 4). With one constraint and a scalar report, only two cases need computing: fully slack and binding (Proposition 6).

section: 7 How it relates to prior work
text:
7 How it relates to prior work
Factor-model inference usually fixes rotation and scale by a normalization. This paper asks what that normalization does to the split among latent, observed-factor and intercept blocks when it is learned from data.









Prior work
What it established
What this paper adds




Bai (2003); Bai and Ng (2013)
Inference and identification for large approximate factor models under normalization restrictions.
A metric-indexed loading class with retained labelled blocks, and root-T theory that allows a fixed cross section, with a covariance-alignment condition linking the profiled target to the structural loading class.


Kelly et al. (2019)
Characteristics instrument time-varying loadings on latent factors (IPCA), with a characteristic-driven intercept and optional observed factors; rotation is fixed by the Euclidean normalization Γβ′Γβ = I.
Treats that normalization as one choice of metric, shows the split across latent, observed-factor and intercept blocks depends on it, and carries an estimated Gram metric into inference.


Newey (1994); Newey and McFadden (1994)
Influence adjustments for estimators that use a first-step estimate.
Applies the two-step correction to a metric that both selects the decomposition and enters the report, keeping the cross-covariance and chart invariance.


Geyer (1994); Andrews (1999); Shapiro (2000)
Limit laws for estimators constrained to a set or near a boundary.
A boundary that is itself learned through the same metric, giving a joint score, boundary and report law.


Andrews and Guggenberger (2009); Andrews and Soares (2010)
Uniformly valid inference when moment inequalities may bind: plug-in (least-favorable) and subsampling critical values, and generalized moment selection, which uses the data to pick the nearly binding inequalities.
For one smooth constraint and a scalar report, the least-favorable envelope reduces to the interior and binding endpoints, so no slack estimate or drift grid is needed.


Li (2025)
A fast bootstrap that consistently estimates, pointwise, the limit law of constrained estimators, with fixed or estimated constraints.
An analytic projection route, uniform over local slack, for the case where the estimated constraint and the estimand share one learned metric.




The angle is measurement, not a new predictor. Geometry on matrix manifolds (Edelman et al. 1998), two-step adjustment and constrained projection are established tools. The contribution is to combine them for one object: a decomposition whose measuring rule is estimated from the same data and may also set its exposure limit. The result is a single influence function that gives the same answer in any admissible local coordinates. For one smooth constraint and a scalar report, it also gives an interval near a learned limit that does not require knowing whether the limit binds, at the cost of some conservativeness and length.
An earlier, broader treatment of the identification question is A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models. The companion paper Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice applies the matched transformation to portfolios.

title: Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference
text:
8 Scope

The theory is local and finite-dimensional: a regular local branch, an exactly profiled fixed-weight estimator, and smooth reports (Section 9). It does not cover weak identification, a growing number of characteristics, or unverified alternating algorithms (Sections 7.4 and 9).
The report-inference theorem is not inference for rolling portfolio Sharpe ratios or for risk premia.
The simulation gain is better uncertainty measurement for the same estimate, not better fitted returns (Section 8.2).
The boundary results cover one smooth constraint and a scalar report, not multiple inequalities or vector confidence regions (Section 7.3).
The intercept is the part of fitted return left outside the factor blocks. Reading it as a pricing error needs a specified pricing model (Section 2).

title: 特征几何与投资组合选择
text:
1 研究问题
当因子模型的预测被转化为投资组合时，度量特征暴露所用的“单位”会怎样改变投资者的实际持仓？
IPCA (Kelly 等 2019) 等基于特征的因子模型，让股票对各因子的暴露随其市值、账面市值比等特征变化。估计这类模型，必须先规定“一个单位的暴露”是什么意思、两个暴露在什么情况下算互不相关。这一规定在数学上是特征空间上的一个度量（metric），论文形象地称之为“尺子”。换尺子不会改变拟合收益。论文要问的是：它会不会改变投资组合？另一项建模选择，即在预期收益中保留拟合出的截距，又会给组合带来什么？

title: 特征几何与投资组合选择
text:
2 为什么重要
学界通常以预测好坏来比较因子模型，而投资者持有的是组合。任何量化策略都要借助风险模型把预测变成头寸，而风险模型有自己的单位和正则化规则。如果这些约定本身就能改变持仓，持仓的变化就可能被误读为新信息。

经济含义。 预测相差约百万分之五，两组组合权重的余弦相似度中位数却只有 0.83（1 表示方向完全相同）（幻灯片 9）。这一差距并非来自不同的预测。
实务含义。 风险模型度量或正则化因子暴露的方式一旦改变，即使没有新的预测，头寸也可能随之变化。弄清差异的来源，基金经理才知道在把持仓变化当作信号之前应当固定哪些设定。
统计含义。 特征库高度拥挤。在 618 个月里，这 132 个特征的变化只相当于约 20 个同等重要的方向：参与维数的中位数为 19.8（幻灯片 7）。因此，如何度量这种重叠是一项实质性的建模选择。
截距的投资价值。 只用因子部分构建的组合会舍弃拟合出的截距。在同一拟合内度量这一输入的价值，可以把它与“更好的模型”带来的价值区分开。

title: 特征几何与投资组合选择
text:
3 论证脉络


问题。 在预测不变的情况下，模型度量特征暴露的方式能否改变投资组合？→ 研究问题
动机。 投资者持有的是组合而非预测；改变持仓的单位约定可能被误读为新信息。→ 为什么重要
框架。 数据只确定每只股票的拟合收益；尺子只决定如何拆分、以什么单位表示（幻灯片 6、A13）。→ 理论框架
机制。 加在因子方差上的固定岭调整 0.01，换了单位就成了不同的个股层面惩罚（幻灯片 8、10）。→ 一个简单例子
证据。 只去掉这一岭调整，618 个月的权重差距几乎全部消失；在同一拟合内，保留截距提高了扣费前夏普比率，但 2007 年后的估计不够精确（幻灯片 11、14、15）。→ 研究设计与主要结果
贡献。 针对在因子单位下做正则化的因子组合规则提出一项表示一致性检验，并在同一拟合内度量单一输入的价值。→ 与既有文献的比较
边界。 扣费前不等于扣费后；机制检验不是业绩检验；截距效应的证据在 2007 年后不够精确。→ 适用范围

4 理论框架
模型把每只股票下月的超额收益写成其特征与三个模块系数的乘积：潜在因子模块、Fama-French 五因子构成的可观测因子模块，以及一个不随任何因子变动的截距模块（幻灯片 4）：

r_{i,s+1} = z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\beta f_{s+1} + z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\delta g_{s+1} + z_{i,s}'\Gamma_\alpha + \varepsilon_{i,s+1}.

其中 z_{i,s} 是股票 i 的特征向量，f 为三个潜在因子，g 为可观测因子，各个 \Gamma 把特征映射为载荷。数据只能确定三个模块之和；这个和如何拆分，取决于尺子，即度量矩阵，它规定载荷方向的“单位长度”。IPCA 使用单位矩阵度量（即“普通尺子”），把每个特征都当作一条独立、等尺度的坐标轴。QZ-IPCA 使用特征格拉姆（Gram）度量，即各特征两两乘积在股票截面上的平均；在这把尺子下，只有当两个载荷方向所产生的个股暴露在截面上的平均乘积为零时，才算互不相关（幻灯片 5、6）。
论文在每个 120 个月的估计窗口内用三种方式构造格拉姆度量：半衰期 60 个月的指数加权平均（EWMA）、120 个月等权平均，以及最近 60 个月的平均（滚动 60）（幻灯片 A14）。机制检验均采用 EWMA 尺子；图 3 展示的是滚动 60 尺子。NA-IPCA 在此基础上加入拟合截距，并设 0.035 的规模上限，该上限在本样本中从未触及（幻灯片 13、A2）。
换尺子相当于一次匹配的单位换算：载荷被重新标度，重叠部分在各模块之间转移，因子序列相应补偿，所有拟合收益和残差都保持不变（幻灯片 6、A13）。一般理论见配套的理论论文 (Liu 2026)。
所有模型都使用同一个均值-方差规则，并为数值稳定在每个因子方差和每只股票方差上各加 0.01 的岭调整（幻灯片 8）。展开来看，该规则选择权重 w 以求解（幻灯片 8、10）

\max_w \; w'\hat\mu \;-\; \tfrac12\, w'A_0\, w \;-\; \tfrac{\lambda_F}{2}\,\lVert B'w\rVert^2 ,

其中 \hat\mu 为预测收益，A_0 为去掉因子岭调整后的风险矩阵，B'w 为组合对各因子的暴露，\lambda_F = 0.01 为岭参数。在预测和因子协方差随载荷一同变换时，前两项在换尺子后严格不变（幻灯片 A13）；最后一项按各因子自身的单位对暴露收费，因此会变（幻灯片 10）。最后，头寸按多空绝对值之和为一美元进行缩放（幻灯片 8）。

表明载荷归一化方式虽不影响拟合，却会通过固定的因子岭调整改变组合；就截距而言，本文在同一拟合内（三个潜在因子加 FF5）度量有上限约束的截距在扣费前的组合价值，并不重新检验其零截距约束


Gu 等 (2020)
基于大量特征的机器学习预测能为投资者带来可观收益
在预测几乎不变时，组合仍会随风险模型的正则项而改变：预测一致并不意味着组合一致


Lettau and Pelger (2020)
在 PCA 中加入均值拟合惩罚，可找回对预期收益重要的因子（RP-PCA）
在同一规则下把 RP-PCA 作为基准；改变的是模型输出的使用方式，而非估计方法


Jagannathan and Ma (2003)
组合权重约束的作用类似协方差收缩
因子方差上的岭调整相当于一个个股层面的暴露惩罚，其形式取决于因子单位


Ledoit and Wolf (2017)
非线性协方差收缩可改进组合选择
因子空间的正则项只有随坐标一同换算，或直接在个股空间设定，才能保持含义不变


Zaffaroni (2025)
在大截面条件因子模型中，渐近无套利意味着定价误差总体上很小（平方可和），而非每个截距为零；遗漏因子会使 alpha 的解读更困难
约束截距的暴露规模并度量其组合价值，不把它断言为错误定价


Brandt 等 (2009)
组合权重可直接设为特征的函数，无需协方差矩阵
本文的组合要经过因子模型和因子协方差，因子岭调整的渠道正是从这里进入；在他们的设计中这一渠道并不存在




本文的贡献较为具体，共有三点。第一，一个代数观察：不影响拟合的归一化选择，会通过固定的因子岭调整进入组合决策，补救办法也很简单，即让岭调整随坐标换算，或直接在个股空间设定。第二，一项基于存档矩阵的实验，在 618 个月中逐月证实了这一渠道（幻灯片 11、A10）。第三，一项同一拟合内的消融分析，度量保留截距在扣费前的投资价值。任何基于因子的组合规则都可以用它来检验；它不是一种新的估计方法。

text:
8 适用范围

扣费前不等于扣费后。 所有夏普比率都未扣除交易、融资和融券成本，并按总敞口归一；图 3 中的成本曲线只是代理（幻灯片 8、A30）。
去掉岭调整是机制检验，不是业绩检验。 论文并未计算无岭调整或换算岭调整后组合的收益（幻灯片 11、A13）。
重叠不等于被定价风险的个数。 格拉姆度量及其参与维数衡量的是特征暴露的重叠程度，而不是有多少风险被定价（幻灯片 5、7）。
未证明截距是错误定价或套利机会。 截距带来的头寸可能含有因子暴露；作定价解释需要一个明确设定的因子定价基准；近期结果较弱，本身也不足以说明发生了结构性变化（幻灯片 15、A32）。
没有确立最优的尺子。 论文报告了三种格拉姆尺子的构造，未按显著性挑选；置信区间均为逐点区间，未针对多重比较作调整（幻灯片 A15 至 A17）。

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
1 研究问题
基于特征的因子模型在拟合收益时，是什么决定了拟合值在潜在因子、可观测因子与截距之间的划分？这种划分又能被估计得多精确？
IPCA（工具化主成分分析）一类模型让规模、价值、动量等公司特征决定每只股票的因子载荷。当潜在因子与可观测因子、截距同时存在时，潜在因子的变动可以抵消载荷在各模块之间的重新分配，而每一个拟合收益都保持不变（第 1 节）。许多特征还彼此重叠：两个价值信号往往选中同一批股票，这使划分规则的选择变得至关重要。

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
2 为什么重要
研究者经常报告潜在因子对某个基准的暴露有多大、残余截距有多大、潜在因子张成了哪些特征方向。这些数字都取决于划分方式，而不只取决于拟合值本身。

经济含义。 在拟合收益完全相同的情况下，同一个基准暴露或截距，用一把尺子看很大，换一把尺子看可能很小（命题 1）。
实务含义。 残差平方和与 R² 只依赖拟合值，因此无法在不同尺子之间作出选择（推论 1）。
统计含义。 本文所用的尺子是特征格拉姆（Gram）矩阵的样本均值，它本身由数据估计。把它当作已知，会遗漏度量带来的方差项及其与收益得分的协方差（定理 1）；在论文的模拟中，这会使标准误偏小（第 8.2 节）。

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
3 论证脉络


问题。 用什么规则把同一个拟合收益分给潜在因子、可观测因子和截距？→ 研究问题
动机。 报告的暴露随规则而变，拟合却不变，所以拟合指标无法选定规则。→ 为什么重要
框架。 特征空间上的内积（即度量）选定这一划分；换一个度量，拟合被重新拆分，但任何拟合收益都不变。→ 理论框架
机制。 改变度量会在各模块之间挪动拟合收益，而总和不变。度量由同一面板数据估计，其估计误差会传入所报告的暴露，并可能改变暴露上限。→ 一个简单例子
证据。 真实特征中有相当一部分暴露彼此重叠，谱结构集中；模拟显示，忽略度量误差会降低覆盖率；在需要估计的上限附近，漂移稳健区间能保持覆盖率。→ 研究设计与主要结果
贡献。 一个计入“尺子”估计误差、且不随模型参数化方式改变的标准误公式；以及在暴露上限附近无论上限是否起约束作用都保持有效的置信区间。→ 与既有文献的比较
边界。 理论是局部的，假定模型在某个解附近强识别，适用于光滑的报告量。→ 适用范围

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
4 理论框架
在每一期，股票 i 具有特征 z_{i,t} 和下一期的超额收益。模型包含三个模块（式 2.1）：

r_{i,t+1} = z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\beta f_{t+1} + z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\delta g_{t+1} + z_{i,t}'\Gamma_\alpha + \varepsilon_{i,t+1}.

其中 f 为潜在因子，g 为可观测因子，\Gamma_\alpha 是由特征驱动的截距。要把各模块分开，就必须先规定两个载荷方向何时算“重叠”。格拉姆度量用两个方向在股票上生成的暴露来衡量重叠（式 2.5）：

\langle a,b\rangle_{Q_Z} = a'Q_Z\,b = \mathbb{E}\!\left[N_t^{-1}(Z_t a)'(Z_t b)\right].

两个系数向量在纸面上可以相互垂直，实际却买入同一批股票；按这把尺子衡量，它们是重叠的。
理论分三步展开。

识别。 对任意正定度量，一个匹配变换先把潜在载荷标准化，再去掉其他模块与潜在方向的重叠，并在因子序列中抵消这两步改动，所有拟合收益保持不变（命题 1）。因此推断对象是去除潜在旋转后的载荷类；总体准则的局部曲率保证它可以被识别（命题 2）。协方差对齐条件（连同局部正则条件）是一个充分条件：即使截面规模固定，它也能保证这一目标就是结构载荷类（命题 3）。
度量需要估计时的推断。 估计量是精确轮廓化（exactly profiled）的：给定载荷，每期用最小二乘求出因子，各期权重固定。在正则的局部分支上（即某个性质良好的解附近），其 \sqrt{T} 大样本展开在通常的收益项之外加入度量估计项，并保留二者的协方差（定理 1）。光滑的报告量，例如与某一特征方向的对齐程度、与基准子空间的距离、截距暴露，继承同一个影响函数。影响函数刻画每一期数据对估计值的影响；由它可以得到一个不随模型参数化方式改变的抽样误差公式（定理 2）；用标准 HAC（异方差与自相关稳健）方法估计其长期方差，即可得到渐近有效的置信区间（命题 5）。
需要估计的暴露上限。 模型可以用预算限制截距暴露。在上限附近，估计的度量不仅改变得分，还会移动可行集边界，因此抽样分布是一个投影，而不是对称的正态分布（定理 3）。基于最不利分位数（即在未知松弛程度中取对覆盖率最不利情形下的临界值）构造的区间，在渐近意义下对未知的松弛程度一致地达到至少名义覆盖率，但可能偏保守（定理 4）。当只有一个约束、报告量为标量时，只需计算完全松弛和约束为紧（binding）两种情形（命题 6）。

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
7 与既有文献的比较
因子模型推断通常用一个标准化约束固定旋转与尺度。本文追问：当这一标准化所依赖的度量需要由数据估计时，它会如何影响潜在因子、可观测因子与截距模块之间的划分。









既有研究
已有结论
本文的补充




Bai (2003)；Bai and Ng (2013)
在标准化约束下，为大维近似因子模型建立识别与推断理论。
以度量为索引、并保留可观测因子与截距模块的载荷类，允许截面规模固定的 \sqrt{T} 理论，并给出协方差对齐条件，使轮廓化目标与结构载荷类一致。


Kelly 等 (2019)
以特征作为潜在因子时变载荷的工具变量（IPCA），模型包含由特征决定的截距与可选的可观测因子；旋转由欧氏标准化 Γβ′Γβ = I 固定。
把这一标准化视为度量的一种选择，说明潜在因子、可观测因子与截距之间的划分取决于该选择，并把估计出的格拉姆度量纳入推断。


Newey (1994)；Newey and McFadden (1994)
为使用第一步估计量的两步估计提供影响函数修正。
把两步修正用于一个既决定分解、又进入报告量的度量，同时保留交叉协方差与坐标不变性。


Geyer (1994)；Andrews (1999)；Shapiro (2000)
参数受约束或位于边界附近时估计量的极限分布。
边界本身通过同一度量被估计，由此得到得分、边界与报告量的联合极限分布。


Andrews and Guggenberger (2009)；Andrews and Soares (2010)
矩不等式可能为紧时的一致有效推断：插入式（最不利）临界值与子抽样，以及用数据挑选接近为紧的不等式的广义矩选择法。
在单一光滑约束和标量报告量下，最不利包络只需内点与紧约束两个端点，无需估计松弛程度，也无需搜索漂移网格。


Li (2025)
一种快速自助法，可逐点一致地估计约束估计量（约束固定或需估计）的极限分布。
当被估计的约束与估计对象共用同一个学习得到的度量时，给出对局部松弛程度一致有效的解析投影方法。




本文的切入点是度量问题，而不是提出新的预测变量。矩阵流形上的几何 (Edelman 等 1998)、两步估计修正和约束投影都是成熟工具；本文的贡献在于把它们结合起来，处理同一个对象：一种分解，其度量规则由同一数据估计，并可能同时设定暴露上限。由此得到的影响函数在任何容许的局部坐标下结果相同；对单一光滑约束和标量报告量，在需要估计的上限附近，所给区间无需事先判断约束是否为紧，代价是区间偏保守、更长。
关于同一识别问题更早、范围更广的论述，见《基于特征的因子模型中识别问题的几何框架》。配套论文《特征几何与投资组合选择》把匹配变换的结论应用于投资组合。

title: 因子模型中的特征空间度量：识别与推断
text:
8 适用范围

理论是局部的、有限维的：依赖正则的局部分支、精确轮廓化的固定权重估计量和光滑的报告量（第 9 节）。弱识别、特征维数增长以及未经验证的交替算法，均不在本文讨论范围之内（第 7.4 节与第 9 节）。
关于报告量的推断定理并不适用于滚动投资组合的夏普比率或风险溢价。
模拟中的改进在于同一估计量的不确定性度量更准确，而不是拟合收益更好（第 8.2 节）。
边界结果只针对单一光滑约束和标量报告量，不涵盖多个不等式约束或向量置信域（第 7.3 节）。
截距是拟合收益中未归入因子模块的部分；要把它解读为定价误差，需要先设定一个定价模型（第 2 节）。
